affected_areas.evidence: New services build analysis context from GitHub Pull Request data and the QA catalog, call the OpenAI Responses API, and write versioned report, latest, and index JSON artifacts under public/ai.

affected_areas.area: GitHub Actions automation and artifact branch publishing
affected_areas.evidence: The added generate-ai-report workflow runs after merged Pull Requests targeting main, restores ai-reports history, generates a report, and commits public/ai artifacts to the ai-reports branch using contents: write permission.
app.py adds GET /api/ai-reports and GET /api/ai-reports/<int:pr_number>, with controlled response envelopes and status mappings for unavailable, malformed, and missing upstream report data.

A new /ai route, ai_assisted_qa.html, ai_assisted_qa.js, and substantial CSS additions render persisted reports, report selection, tabs, risk indicators, changed-file summaries, and unavailable states.

The AI report feed service validates report/index fields, fixed report paths, change-summary totals, and optional public changed-file metadata; the browser script validates report structure and constrains GitHub Pull Request links.

affected_areas.area: QA catalog and controlled AI evaluation
affected_areas.evidence: The new AST-based QA context service derives product-suite test metadata, while evaluation cases and evaluator logic assess grounding, risk calibration, incomplete-evidence limitations, and resistance to embedded prompt-injection text.
Navigation links to /ai are added to multiple templates, the Test Library gains AI report UI cases, and README/About content documents the new reporting architecture and operational boundaries.

analysis_limitations: The supplied change summary reports 36 changed files, while the provided changed-file evidence does not clearly include all 36 files; impact assessment is limited to the visible file and patch evidence.
No CI logs, GitHub Actions run results, deployed-environment results, generated report artifacts, or live OpenAI/GitHub integration evidence were supplied.
Several patches are partial diffs rather than complete source files, so behavior outside the changed snippets cannot be fully assessed.

The existing QA catalog identifies test names and source locations but does not provide complete assertions for every pre-existing test; relevance is based on catalog metadata and the changed test evidence only.
analysis.change_summary: This Pull Request adds an AI-assisted Pull Request change-impact feature spanning GitHub PR ingestion, source-derived QA catalog discovery, structured OpenAI analysis, persisted report artifacts, a GitHub Actions generation workflow, read-only Flask report APIs, and a browser-based /ai report explorer. It also adds deterministic evaluation scenarios and supporting documentation, dependency, navigation, styling, and test-library updates.

coverage_gaps.area: Merged-PR GitHub Actions generation and ai-reports branch publication
coverage_gaps.reason: The catalog contains route and UI coverage for consuming persisted reports, but no catalog test covers the workflow’s merged-PR trigger, report-history restoration, generation invocation, idempotent no-change path, or push to the artifact branch.

coverage_gaps.area: Flask invalid Pull Request number handling
coverage_gaps.reason: The detail route has an explicit non-positive PR-number response branch, but no supplied catalog test covers GET /api/ai-reports/0 and its expected controlled 400 response.

The route catalog covers unavailable, missing-report, and invalid-report responses, but app.py also maps invalid_json, invalid_index, and upstream_http_error errors without corresponding catalog entries.
The browser implementation supports ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Home, and End navigation for tabs, while the supplied UI test evidence shows click-based tab checks only.

The supplied catalog covers mocked or intercepted boundaries. It does not establish behavior against live GitHub API responses, OpenAI service responses, GitHub Actions secrets, or the deployed raw artifact feed.

qa_notes: The new product-facing catalog entries provide direct route and browser coverage for primary available and unavailable report-explorer states.
The feature separates model-generated analysis from deterministic report provenance and change statistics; this is an important boundary to retain in future changes.

The PR description includes validation and live-evaluation statements, but no execution logs or workflow artifacts were supplied here; this analysis does not treat those statements as verified test results.

Supporting service-level tests are present in the changed-file evidence, but they are intentionally excluded from the supplied product-facing QA catalog and are therefore not cited as relevant existing catalog tests.

analysis.risk_rationale: Risk is high because the change introduces a large new cross-cutting capability (6,432 reported line changes across 36 files) with external GitHub and OpenAI dependencies, CI write access to an artifact branch, new public Flask endpoints, persisted report-data validation, and a client-rendered reporting surface. The implementation includes controlled error handling, schema restrictions, and tests, but correctness depends on integration boundaries that are broader than the existing product-facing QA catalog.
